auditor_value: (a) x₀ = −20 m; (b) v = +2 m/s; (c) x = (−20 + 2t) m; (d) uniform velocity, reaches the origin at t = 10 s

findings.quote: The particle starts at x = −20 m and moves with a constant velocity of +2 m/s (zero acceleration), reaching x = 0 m at t = 10 s; it is in uniform motion in the positive x-direction throughout.
findings.note: Part (c) asks for the position as a function of time, and neither the steps nor the final answer ever writes it. A student following this solution has nothing to write for that sub-part.
findings.fix: Add the equation of motion: x = x₀ + vt = (−20 + 2t) m, then state the rest as written.

findings.quote: Taking the slope as 20/10 without checking the sign of the intercept gives the wrong starting position.
findings.note: The stated cause cannot produce the stated error. 20/10 = +2 m/s is the correct slope and correct velocity, and a slope calculation does not fix the starting position, which is read directly off the intercept.
findings.fix: Reading the intercept as +20 m instead of −20 m, because only the size of the marking is read and not its sign, gives the wrong starting position and the wrong equation x = 20 + 2t.
